bull.b: Sustained, very high TPV growth and multiple quarters above 50% reflect strong merchant adoption, broad geographic expansion and network effects. Large and growing TPV supports durable fee revenue, strengthens partner relationships, and increases scale advantages across emerging markets.

Solid operating and net margins combined with very high ROE indicate efficient capital use and strong unit economics. Low leverage amplifies return sustainability and provides flexibility to fund growth without materially increasing financial risk, supporting long-term shareholder returns.

bull.t: Strong Cash Generation & Conservative Balance Sheet
bull.b: Robust TTM operating and free cash flow with cash conversion near 1x of net income shows earnings quality and internal funding capacity. Combined with a conservative balance sheet, this durability supports strategic investments, weathering cycles, and the ability to self-fund expansion in emerging markets.

bear.b: A material decline in gross margin versus prior periods signals growing cost pressure or lower monetization on certain payment rails. If persistent, this erodes operating leverage and requires higher growth or sustained cost control to preserve profitability and return metrics over the medium term.

bear.t: Elevated Operating Expenses from Investment Cycle
bear.b: A large YoY jump in operating expenses reflects an intensive investment cycle. While intended to drive growth, prolonged elevated OpEx can delay operating leverage recovery and compress margins unless productivity gains or revenue uplift materialize as expected in H2 and beyond.

bear.t: Cash Flow Volatility & Working Capital Risks
bear.b: Past negative OCF/FCF and recent working-capital timing issues show cash conversion can swing materially. Persistent receivable or merchant-advance timing risks could stress liquidity or force financing, making cash generation less predictable over the medium term despite strong TTM aggregates.
